answer: Yes, two solid materials have been burned in this window [limits:headline]. These were SIBAL Cloth at 31.0 mol % O2 and 54.1 kPa, and Two-Sided PMMA at 30.3 mol % and 54.6 kPa, both at 20.0 cm/s airflow [limits:headline]. The source describes Moon-base air as at least 30% O2 at 10.2 psi (70.33 kPa) or less [limits:headline]. Every point in this window is from microgravity, with no partial-gravity combustion data [limits:gaps:moon_base].

chunks.text: Of the solid-material space fire tests in our sources, only 2 burned in Moon-base air (Saffire VI-2, SIBAL Cloth, 31.0 mol % at 54.1 kPa, 20.0 cm/s; Saffire VI-3, Two-Sided PMMA, 30.3 mol % at 54.6 kPa, 20.0 cm/s), none in partial gravity. Moon-base air means at least 30% O2 at 10.2 psi (70.33 kPa) or less, from the challenge page.

The intermediate oxygen concentration used on the Moon will likely be 30% or greater, with a corresponding pressure of 10.2 psi or less. Compared to Earth’s atmosphere, that’s more than a 40% increase in the oxygen concentration making materials much more flammable.

chunks.source: Flame Frontier Known Limits: Space Apps challenge page
chunks.text: Space Apps challenge page gives: Mission context: spacesuit 100% O2 at 4.3 psi; Moon base / rovers at 30%+ O2 and 10.2 psi or less; no partial-gravity combustion data in PSI. It does not give: ACME CFI-G gas-flame tests reached higher O2: "an oxygen-nitrogen mixture of up to 85% oxygen flowed from the spherical burner creating an inside-out flame" (sec. 1). That is the burner's oxidizer stream, not a chamber atmosphere, and not solid materials. Kept off the charts. No lower pressure bound for the Moon-base zone, so the zone is drawn down to 0 kPa.

chunks.text: Pressurized rover target: ≥30% O2 at ≤70.3 kPa, partial gravity. 2 solid-material tests in this window. Inside ≥30% O2 at ≤70.3 kPa, solids were burned at 20 cm/s airflow only; no solid test in this window at any other flow. Flow is not an axis on Panel 1: every point in the highlighted box shares that flow. Only 2 solid materials burned in ≥30% O2 at ≤70.3 kPa: SIBAL Cloth; Two-Sided PMMA. No flammability boundary (where a solid stops burning) was measured in ≥30% O2 at ≤70.3 kPa. The only one in our data, BASS-II eq. 6.1 for PMMA rods, was measured at 101.3 kPa. No combustion test at partial gravity: every point on both panels is from microgravity. Challenge page: "there is currently no partial-gravity combustion data available in PSI". 2 solid-material tests had O2 and pressure in ≥30% O2 at ≤70.3 kPa: Saffire VI-2, Saffire VI-3. Non-solid tests in ≥30% O2 at ≤70.3 kPa: 20 CFI-G gas flames, 0 FLEX liquid droplets. They do not close a solid-material gap.

chunks.source: PSI-99 Spacecraft Fire Experiment-II: PSI metadata Comment[Approach]
chunks.text: The Saffire-II experiment was performed on the Orbital Science’s Cygnus resupply vehicle after it deberthed from the ISS. As a follow on to the Saffire-I investigation, the Saffire-II investigation added more samples including SIBAL, silicone, structure PMMA, flat PMMA, and PMMA with Nomex. The Saffire-1I flight unit had a sample card installed in the middle of a large flow duct. Air is drawn through the flow duct by fans located at the top of the duct with flow straighteners at the bottom of the experiment module. Saffire-II has a sample card that contains 9 samples, each 5 cm x 29 cm. Depending on the sample material, the Saffire-II was conducted at an air flow velocity of either 20 or 30 cm/s, the flow being either concurrent or opposed. Once the sample was ignited flame images were captured using two cameras. In addition, thermocouples provided flow, flame, and plume temperatures, two radiometers recorded flame radiation, solid state sensors were used to measure pressure, CO2 and O2 mole faction, and two anemometer tracked flow velocity.

question: Has any solid material been burned in Moon-base air, at 30% oxygen or more and 10.2 psi or less?
